seo_description: Hold Command to see every menu shortcut of the frontmost Mac app, or search and run them with a hotkey. Free, open source, native, no network access.
hero_sub: Hold Command alone for a moment and an overlay lists the frontmost app's menu shortcuts. Press Control-Option-Command-K to search them and run any item.
features_sub: A small menu bar app that reads the menus you already have and shows what each shortcut does.

features.title: Hold Command to peek
features.desc: Hold Command alone for 0.8, 1.2 or 2 seconds and a centered overlay appears. Release the key and it disappears.

features.title: No false triggers
features.desc: The hold is cancelled by any other key, modifier, click or scroll, so ordinary shortcuts like Command-C never flash the overlay.

features.title: Search and run menu items
features.desc: A global hotkey opens a search window. Type to filter by item or menu name, then press Return to run the selected item.

features.title: Grouped by menu
features.desc: Shortcuts appear as keycap glyphs, grouped by File, Edit, View and the rest in menu-bar order. Disabled items are dimmed.

features.title: Favorites per app
features.desc: Star the items you use and they are pinned to the top, in both search and hold mode.

features.title: Excluded apps and settings
features.desc: Choose apps where the overlay never shows, record your own hotkey, and optionally launch at login. The overlay is skipped during secure input.

permissions_step: When prompted, grant Accessibility access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility.

faq.q: Is ShortcutPeekOverlay really free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is released under the MIT license and the full source is on GitHub. There are no ads, accounts or paid tiers, and an optional Support button links to Ko-fi.

Accessibility, which it uses to read the frontmost app's menus, press the item you choose, and listen for the Command hold and hotkey with a listen-only event tap. It never blocks or records keystrokes, and macOS may also list it under Input Monitoring. Launch at login is optional.
Settings and favorites are stored locally on your Mac in the app's preferences. The app makes no network connections and has no analytics. Menu data is cached in memory for 5 seconds per app.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to get past Gatekeeper, or build it yourself from source.
